To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a simple service that provides application developers with the network information needed to optimize their applications can enable network-aware applications; and 2) the service can be built on top of existing network monitoring tools.

1) the network is often the bottleneck for distributed high-performance applications; 2) network tuning techniques exist that can dramatically improve application performance; 3) these techniques are not widely used; 4) a network-aware application service can make the task of network configuration trivial for users; and 5) such a service should be widely adopted to eliminate a common stumbling-block for high-performance distributed application developers.

(1) the current state of the art for network tuning is inadequate; (2) a network tuning service that uses a simple interface and is easy to use will enable the development of network-aware applications; (3) such a service can be implemented using existing technologies, such as the TCP tuning service and the TCP buffer tuning service, which are available in many Unix systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the networking community has developed a set of best practices for tuning the network stack that are not widely known or used by the application development community.
network tuning can be automated to a great degree, and this can greatly increase the performance of distributed applications.
the networking community should work more closely with the application development community to ensure that the full potential of high-speed networks is realized.
